evidence.quote:
Trade-off hacking: Have the cake and eat it too? Turning competing interests into win-wins
in data-driven food technology

General comments:
The work addresses a real and highly topical problem. It is highly relevant to policy design.
However, there are some areas that need improvement.
○

Abstract
It is not specified how the pilot projects were explicitly analyzed.
○

Introduction
This section contains statements heavily biased towards justifying the project. It would be
preferable for it to be more neutral.
○

Background
Trade-off hacking: this concept should be expanded upon as much as possible. It would be
beneficial to explore the issues further.
Regarding the trade-offs, it would be helpful to explain why there were only three.
○

○

Trade-off hacking: vignettes from the DRG4FOOD pilots
This section would be strengthened if it were more critical. Furthermore, it would be
advisable to include failures, unresolved tensions, and aspects not yet considered.
○

Synthesis: Two patterns of trade-off hacking
In this section, it would be advisable to delve deeper into the limitations of each of the
patterns. It should be more critical.
○




Discussion
This section seems too closely aligned with the project objectives. A more critical analysis is
needed; otherwise, there is a risk of analytical bias. What would happen without funding?
What would happen if an attempt were made to replicate the study? What aspects are most
important to consider? What happens outside the contexts of the analysis?
○

Conclusions
This section is very encouraging. It shows a positive bias. It needs to be more critical.
○

Yes

Thank you for the constructive feedback. The manuscript has been revised to improve
clarity, balance, and critical reflection. Abstract
The description of how pilot material was analysed has been clarified by stating the overall
approach, data basis, and main analytical process more directly. Introduction
The tone has been revised to be more neutral and analytical, with less project-affirming
language. Background (trade-off hacking and trade-off selection)
The conceptual discussion of trade-off hacking has been expanded, and clearer rationale




has been added for focusing on the three main trade-offs in scope. Pilot vignette section
A stronger critical dimension has been added through discussion of unresolved tensions
and aspects that may remain challenging in practice. Synthesis section
More explicit reflection has been included on the limitations and conditions of the identified
patterns. Discussion
The critical analysis has been deepened, including reflections on likely constraints in other
implementation settings. Conclusions
The conclusion has been revised to a more cautious framing, with clearer acknowledgement
of limits and open questions.
